newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hebron Jews protest against Palestinian market.
newsitem.headline: Hebron Jews protest against Palestinian market.

text.p: Israeli soldiers stopped about 20 Jewish settlers from protesting on Thursday against the reopening of the Palestinian produce market in Hebron provided under a peace deal, witnesses said.
Israel partly reopened the market on Wednesday, three years after closing it over a settler's massacre of 29 worshippers at al-Ibrahimi mosque.
Israel last month handed over 80 percent of the volatile West Bank town to PLO self-rule under a U.S.-brokered peace deal and promised to reopen the market.
Witnesses said Palestinians were trying to resume clean-up and renovations at the market situated in the Israeli-held part of Hebron.
Soldiers dispersed the settlers but stopped Palestinian merchants and telephone company workers from resuming renovations, the witnesses said.
"We came to open our stores but the soldiers stopped us from going inside," said Hassan Dais, who owns a shop in the market. He said soldiers gave no explanation for the action.
An Israeli army spokeswoman said she was checking the report. Hebron municipal officials said nine shops would be renovated before merchants resumed business.
